name: Tatami
desc: A tatami floor running away to a hazed horizon — woven igusa rush mats bound in dark cloth borders, laid to the auspicious rule that four mats may never meet at a point, their grain catching a low light that drifts up and down the room.

energy.doc: light contrast + grain/border weight + walk rate

scale.doc: mat size vs frame — drops the eye toward the floor so the mats loom (2.2 = kneeling on them)

density.doc: how many rows of mats recede before the haze takes them

weave.doc: igusa rush grain ruled along each mat's long axis

border.doc: the heri — dark cloth binding on the mats' long edges

x.doc: vanishing point x as canvas fraction

style.doc: aesthetic: natural woven igusa in warm light / tonal sumi ink wash / cold blue night room / sun-bleached and stained with age / luminous additive mat outlines on black (non-representational)

seed.doc: the mat layout itself — re-solves the tatami tiling, plus per-mat grain and ageing
